1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.
LAC no. 136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 2.

entities.text: Tej Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 U/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 Bighas 01 Biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 16//5 (416), 6 min(210) i.e. total area measuring 07 Bigha and 06 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
LAC no. 136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 5.

entities.text: Tej Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioner aggrieved by the market value determined by the LAC, vide the subject award announced on 06.02.2006 while accepting the compensation under protest, challenged the said Award on the grounds as detailed in the reference petition which are summarized as under: -
(i) The ld. LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
The market value as assessed by Land Acquisition Collector is imaginary and based upon the Govt. Policy.

The market value of the acquired land and the market value of the construction/
structure can't be fixed on the basis of any such policy of the Government.

The market value of the acquired land is to be assessed strictly as provided by law within Tejpal Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82063025/
2 the purview of Section 23 and 24 of Land Acquisition Act.

entities.text: Tejpal Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The Land Acquisition Collector have not taken into consideration the future potentiality of the land and should have determined the market value by keeping in view the market value as fixed by the Government for allotment of residential plots/ flats.
The Ld. LAC should have adjusted some amount towards the development charges and assessed the market value of the said land accordingly.

(iv) The DDA with the approval of Govt. of India had issued the guidelines through which DDA has increased the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750/- per sq. yards to Rs. 5,000/- (approx) per sq.
yards.
Therefore, the said land of the petitioner has higher potential value than is assessed by the Ld. LAC.

Further the land of the petitioner is very fertile and leveled and it gives commercial crops 2-3 in a year and yielded high income for the LAC no. 136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 petitioners, without any depression or defect.

entities.text: Tej Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore,
the said land hardly needs any development to be done to make it fit for use as a developed site and it can be used for industrial, commercial or residential use with very little efforts.

(iv) All the amentities and facilities of life like water, electricity, metalled roads, general market, post office, transport facilities, banking facility, hospitals, Engg. College, schools, telephone exchange,
police station are very near to GTK Road, Rohtak Road, Narela Anaj Mandi adjacent to the Narela township which was urbanized in the year 1922 and having commercial as well as Narela industrial area is very near Bawana Industrial Area much prior to the date of notification U/s 4 of the Act

but the LAC did not consider this fact while passing the said award.
(v) There are many palatial farm houses in the close vicinity of the revenue estate of Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari).

The cost of the land of these farmhouses is not less than Rs. 15,000/- sq. yards which also increases the marketable value of the land of the petitioner and the said land is situated on the main road.
The LAC, while passing the award, did not assess the correct value of the standing trees.

(vi) Further, the LAC has ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by the land, other well developed colonies and full approved Industrial areas, etc where the minimum market value of the land is Rs. 10,000/- per sq. yards.

Therefore, the compensation according to the value of land should be valued at Rs. 10,000/- per sq. yards which is the LAC no.
136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 fair actual value of land of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act.

entities.text: Tej Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (vii) The LAC has also erred in not awarding the compensation for the expenses, loss and injury sustained by the petitioner due to competed change of nature and place of business/ livelihood.

The LAC has also not considered the yearly increase of 12% per annum in the value of land between 01.04.2001 to 21.03.2003 i.e. date of policy announced vide order no.F9(20)/L&B/LA/6696 dated 09.08.2001 and the government has also increased the rate of land as 12 % market value of the land prior to the announcement of the above said award however the LAC has not considered the same and the notification U/s 4 of LA Act is a matter of grave concern.

(viii) The petitioner have the tube-well run by diesel/ electric engine in the above said land which was in good condition and working effectively when the possession of the land was taken by the LAC and has grossly erred in not awarding the compensation for boring of the Tube Well and equipment such as pipe, etc.
The value of the standing tree in the land of the petitioner is also not assessed.
6. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioner, petitioner is claiming market value of Rs. 10,000/- per sq. yds.
By placing the land of the petitioner in Category- A alongwith interest in solatium.
The petitioner is also claiming interest at the rate of 24% p.a. on enhanced amount of compensation w.e.f. from the date of notification U/s 4 (1) of the LA Act.

An alternative plot of LAC no. 136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 reasonable size alongwith the cost of structure/ construction of farm house be granted to the petitioner.

2,00,000/- each.

Interest at 24 % p.a. on the amount of compensation withheld by the LAC from the date of award, Rs. 1,00,000/- as damage to standing crop and market value of trees at Rs. 5,000/-
each alongwith other statutory benefits be also granted to the petitioner.

7. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted the Ld. LAC has assessed the fair market value of the said land.
The petition is not maintainable as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence is respect of relief claimed.

The possession of the land measuring 07 Bigha and 06 Biswas as also detailed in the statement U/s 19 of LA Act has been taken by the LAC and handed over to DDA on 04.04.2006 and as such DDA is a necessary party being the beneficiary of the said land.
All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available LAC no. 136/
2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 to Ld. LAC.

entities.text: Tej Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

9. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days
therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.

11. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 14.12.2013 :  ISSUES:
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, then to what amount?

2. Relief.
12.
Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.

Counsel for the petitioners as well as Ld. Counsels for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issuewise findings and determination are as under:  LAC no. 136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 12 1.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, then to what amount?
15. The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.

17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate LAC no. 136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 12 therefrom.

entities.text: Tej Pal v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 21.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: LAC no.
136/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Tej Pal v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 12 (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.

sentences.text: An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
(3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
22.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
